subject: surgery
title: Abdominal Cocoon, Carcinomatosis and Retroperitoneal Disease

steps.tx: Encasement of small bowel loops inside a thick fibrous membrane is called an **abdominal cocoon**. Patients present with repeated episodes of intestinal obstruction, weight loss and a vague abdominal mass. Computed tomography shows clustered bowel loops wrapped in a membrane. Tuberculous peritonitis is an important cause in endemic regions, so the membrane and bowel wall are biopsied during the operation.
steps.say: An abdominal cocoon wraps small bowel in a fibrous membrane and causes repeated bouts of obstruction.

steps.tx: Surgery for an abdominal cocoon centres on careful **membrane excision**. The fibrous sheet is peeled away and the bowel freed without resection whenever possible. Aggressive dissection risks bowel injury, so patience matters more than speed in this operation. An accidental bowel opening during dissection is the main hazard, and a missed injury can turn a benign condition into faecal peritonitis.
steps.say: Cocoon surgery means patiently peeling the membrane away and freeing bowel without resection whenever possible.

steps.tx: Widespread seeding of cancer across the peritoneal surface is termed **peritoneal carcinomatosis**. It commonly comes from stomach, colon, ovarian or appendiceal cancers and causes ascites with progressive obstruction. The extent of seeding guides whether aggressive treatment is worthwhile. Pseudomyxoma peritonei, jelly like mucin from a ruptured appendix, fills the abdomen in some patients and is managed very differently.
steps.say: Peritoneal carcinomatosis seeds cancer across the peritoneum, causing ascites and obstruction from gut or ovarian primaries.

steps.tx: Heated chemotherapy washed through the abdomen during surgery is known as **HIPEC**. It follows complete removal of visible peritoneal tumour in selected patients. The heat increases drug effect on microscopic deposits while limiting exposure to the rest of the body. The wash is heated to about 42 degrees Celsius, and only patients whose visible tumour can be almost completely removed gain benefit.
steps.say: HIPEC washes heated chemotherapy through the abdomen after visible tumour removal to treat microscopic deposits.

steps.tx: Thick fibrous tissue growing around the aorta and ureters is **retroperitoneal fibrosis**. It slowly squeezes the ureters and causes kidney obstruction with vague back pain. Steroids often shrink the tissue, and stents or surgery free trapped ureters. About half of cases have no cause found and are called idiopathic, though IgG4 related disease explains a growing share.
steps.say: Retroperitoneal fibrosis wraps the aorta and ureters, slowly obstructing the kidneys until steroids or stents relieve it.

steps.tx: A fluid filled sac arising within the mesentery is a **mesenteric cyst**. Many cause no symptoms and are found on scans done for other reasons. Large cysts cause pain or obstruction and are removed completely to prevent recurrence. Chylous cysts containing milky lymph are a recognised subtype, and spilling their contents during removal should be carefully avoided.
steps.say: Mesenteric cysts often cause no symptoms, though large ones cause pain or obstruction and need complete removal.

vis.alt: Mesenteric and omental cyst examination showing Tillaux triad mobility.
vis.caption: Mesenteric cyst: mobility across the mesenteric attachment. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Bleeding into the rectus sheath below the arcuate line forms a **rectus sheath haematoma**. It follows coughing, straining or anticoagulant use and causes a painful abdominal wall swelling. The swelling stays palpable when the patient tenses the abdominal muscles. This is the Fothergill sign: a swelling inside the abdomen becomes less palpable when the rectus muscles contract, unlike a sheath haematoma.
steps.say: A rectus sheath haematoma causes a painful wall swelling that stays palpable when the muscles are tensed.

steps.tx: Separation of the two rectus muscles without a true fascial defect is **divarication of recti**. It appears as a midline ridge when the patient sits up and is common after pregnancy. Because there is no narrow neck, strangulation does not occur and surgery is cosmetic only.
steps.say: Divarication of recti is a harmless midline separation after pregnancy, with no neck and no strangulation risk.

steps.tx: A scoring system that maps tumour spread across abdominal regions is the **peritoneal cancer index**. Surgeons use it to judge whether complete tumour removal is feasible. High scores usually mean surgery with heated chemotherapy is unlikely to help. The index divides the abdomen into 13 regions scored 0 to 3 each, giving a maximum total score of 39.
steps.say: The peritoneal cancer index maps tumour spread and helps judge whether complete removal is realistically feasible.
